newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STORK BUYS REST OF FOKKER TECHNOLOGY.
newsitem.headline: STORK BUYS REST OF FOKKER TECHNOLOGY.

text.p: Industrial systems group Stork NV said on Tuesday it had bought the remaining half of Fokker Technology, making the former unit of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker a fully-owned Stork unit.
The deal included patents, designs, raw materials, aircraft parts, production equipment, moulds, an engineering simulator and prototypes of the Fokker 50, Fokker 70 and Fokker 100.

"These purchases, which will raise the profitability of Fokker Aviation, involve an amount of 47.5 million guilders," Stork said. Last year, Stork bought Fokker Aviation, the profitable maintenance and components subsidiary of Fokker.
Stork said that the fact it now owned 100 percent of Fokker Technology had also prematurely ended the buy-back option of Fokker Aviation by Fokker's administrators.
Last year, the administrators demanded the option of buying back Fokker Aviation if they could find a buyer for Fokker's aircraft-making activities with which Stork could or would not cooperate.
Various attempts were made by the receivers to find a suitable buyer for the stricken aircraft maker but all failed.
"The desired integration and further expansion of Fokker Aviation's activities within the Stork group can now be realised without impediment," Stork said.
Stork repeated it expected Fokker Aviation to post 1997 turnover of 800 million guilders on a total Stork group turnover of more than five billion.
In 1996, Fokker Aviation had turnover of about 550 million guilders on a group turnover of 4.92 billion.
